mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: qualified by several curated cards: P4-E-04; EB-KD-01; Track is read only from the card(s) that state it - EB-KD-01 state(s) a route and no Track (written before Track was qualified)
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was newly read in full for these cards. The Lucas-Clarke reading is scientist-a's (receipt FTR-20261026-42909904-01); the compound statements are abstract-level PubMed reads and registry-database retrievals (lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/).
not_known: Whether a WWOX-deficient human neural cell has a measurable bioenergetic defect that a ketone substrate would bypass.
Whether lactate is raised, normal or low in WWOX-deficient human brain across ages and contexts.

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: The fly lactate result is conditional on amyloid and cannot be used for or against the Warburg direction in WWOX-null neurons.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN beyond the empirical seizure-control use.
p4_card.identity: Ketogenic diet (HYP-20260709-01, map record R-05) and, as a direction control only, MCT1 blockade (AZD3965 in DGIdb). No new compound.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: A decision for the treating clinical team, not for this system; this card only records the consequence of the Lucas-Clarke reading: no direct support and no refutation.
p4_card.next_measurement: PDH-specific readouts in donor-derived WWOX-deficient cells or the existing knockout organoids against isogenic controls: PDH activity in a lysate that preserves phosphorylation, phospho-PDHA1 (Ser293, UniProt P08559 precursor numbering; Ser232 and Ser300 are also PDK sites), 13C-glucose or ketone tracing, pyruvate-to-lactate ratio, NADH/NAD+. Seahorse OCR/ECAR is a general screen of respiration and acidification, not a PDH measure, and a normal result in non-neural cells is non-significance, not equivalence; it is useful but not the only discriminating test (HYP-20260709-01, verification 2026-10-27).
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NOT NEW: existing hypothesis, updated with a consequence note on 2026-10-26.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.

scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: Statements marked INFERENZA, including every statement about what a compound would do in WWOX-deficient tissue, are OWED a blind audit by another actor.
scope_of_checks.formal_checks: Disease-side fly rows carry verbatim locators in the manifest (104 entries; entries 31, 49, 89, 94 SUPPORTED by a blind audit, entry 95 narrowed after an OVERSHOOT finding); the compound statements are abstract-level and unaudited.
scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: No independent replication of any fly row is held; the organoid rows are one laboratory's deposit.

external_not_wwox_evidence: DGIdb SLC16A1 rows: AZD3965 (inhibitor), valproic acid and sodium butyrate (no action type)

p4_card.state_of_known_roads: HYP-20260709-01 (ranked, proposed-to-L9), R-05, DL-MECH-020, DL-BIO-008, DL-BIO-009.
p4_card.value_added: Records that this paper changes nothing for the ketogenic hypothesis and names the one measurement that still decides it.

cellular_context.limits: No metabolic readout of the lever exists in a WWOX-deficient human neural system; the lactate rows have opposite signs in the fly (with and without amyloid) and in one human MRS report.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: The existing minimal falsifier of HYP-20260709-01: Seahorse OCR/ECAR on donor-derived cells or the existing organoids; this card adds no new endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: The ketogenic diet in WWOX-DEE: tried in 3 patients in one cohort and continued in 1; a null-genotype report where it was suspended. The Lucas-Clarke study contains no diet, ketone, PDH or pyruvate arm.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: n of 3 and n of 1 clinical reports; fly lactate is amyloid-conditional.

p4_card.identity: Bumetanide (approved loop diuretic). Identity check 2026-10-27: ChEMBL_37 curates its mechanism as inhibition of the NKCC2 transporter only; NKCC1 appears in three activity rows (two single-concentration inhibition readings in HEK cells and one fitted value in HT-29 cells by rubidium uptake), so the NKCC1 target of the repurposing idea is an activity-table fact, not a curated mechanism.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Only IF GABA is depolarising in Wwox-deficient neurons at the relevant age; unmeasured. The CNS penetration of bumetanide is a known limitation (map R-07).
p4_card.mechanism: Target NKCC1 (SLC12A2); wanted direction: lower intracellular chloride so GABA hyperpolarises; sign depends on an unmeasured quantity.
p4_card.next_measurement: Gramicidin perforated-patch E_GABA in Wwox-deficient versus parental neurons or slices at three ages (including the earliest culturable), NKCC1 and KCC2 protein by immunoblot or immunostaining, GABA puff response; controls: wild type and heterozygote, bicuculline or gabazine sensitivity, an NKCC1 knockdown arm in place of the drug; the compound is applied in the bath ex vivo and a systemic arm is not used to test the premise (IT8 P3); discriminating result: a depolarised E_GABA specific to the knockout that an NKCC1 manipulation shifts.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: Map R-07 stands as INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. New: (1) the transcript-level ratio in the one human knockout deposit does not point to a depolarising gradient (descriptive, confounded); (2) the target-identity note above; (3) the single experiment is written out with controls. Neonatal-seizure and autism trials exist (titles retrieved: NEMO open-label dose-finding in newborn hypoxic-ischaemic seizures, PMID 25765333; a phase 3 autism programme, PMID 35292925; a phase 2 autism trial, PMID 32730977); their outcomes were NOT read here.
p4_card.pharmacology: NKCC1 activity: one fitted value and two single-concentration readings in ChEMBL (values in the README). IT8 P3 2026-10-29: GtoPdb (human, one document) gives pIC50 5.60 for NKCC1 and 6.48 for the kidney transporter, so the drug is about 7.6 fold more potent on the renal target; mouse brain to plasma ratio about 0.015 to 0.02 and efflux at the blood-brain barrier (abstract level); a close derivative that does not inhibit NKCC1 reproduces some CNS effects (PMID 30248303), so a CNS effect of the drug is not evidence of NKCC1 action. A systemic arm is therefore not a test of the premise; the drug is applied in the bath ex vivo, where the NKCC1 range of about 1.5 to 2.5 micromolar is the exposure target.
p4_card.predictions: Registered: if GABA is hyperpolarising in the knockout at the age studied, the card closes; if depolarising, bumetanide at a brain-relevant exposure lowers burst frequency, and a negative result at that exposure does not refute the premise.

mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Downstream of an unresolved lesion: even a correct ISR readout would change a consequence, not restore WWOX function. Deep recovery would need WWOX restored (card C01). Track B (Q230P class): whether the missing mutant protein state engages the ISR is not measured; nothing here is lesion-specific.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery
mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class

input.no_new_reading: No paper was newly read in full for these cards. The Lucas-Clarke reading is scientist-a's (receipt FTR-20261026-42909904-01); the compound statements are abstract-level PubMed reads and registry-database retrievals (lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/).
not_known: Whether any WWOX-deficient human neural system has raised eIF2 alpha phosphorylation or ATF4 protein, with or without a proteotoxic load.
Whether the fly Atf4 rise is upstream of Ldh (no Atf4 perturbation in the paper).

Whether the PERK arm or another eIF2 kinase (the paper's Discussion names GCN1/GCN2) is the one engaged; the two interactome entries behind that naming are a low-score unvalidated GCN1 prey (score 0.133, HEK293T) and a three-spectrum WWOX hit in a PERK proximity list (HEK293-T), neither showing binding or activation. In the one fly PARS2 precedent the engaged kinase was GCN2, with phospho-PERK unchanged, so a PERK-arm inhibitor would not be the matched tool there; which kinase, if any, is engaged in WWOX-deficient neural cells is unmeasured.

Whether an eIF2B activator, which acts downstream of eIF2 alpha phosphorylation and restores translation, would reproduce the genetic GCN2 or ATF4 suppression: the fly precedent does not separate the ATF4-dependent limb from the translation-repression limb and tested no compound.
Whether attenuating the ISR would help or harm a WWOX-deficient developing brain.

p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

against: Without amyloid the fly Atf4 comparison was not significant (6 vs 6; no interaction test between backgrounds; not a demonstrated absence).
In the human knockout organoid the ATF4/ISR target transcripts are lower than chance (exploratory, no amyloid).
The ALS trial engaged the target and showed no benefit.
Atf4 is not perturbed in the paper: the Atf4-to-Ldh step is the authors' inference.
The paper reports that Ldh knockdown is detrimental in other fly amyloid models, a reminder that attenuating a stress arm has a cost.
for: The fly reports a raised Atf4 signal with Wwox reduction plus amyloid (n 6, one antibody).
An eIF2B activator improved memory and tau in a mouse amyloid model.
A paediatric dataset for an ISR-attenuating drug exists in a different, eIF2B-driven disease.

GENETIC precedent in another disease (Xu 2026, PMID 41380592; read in full, manifest PMID41380592.json entries 1, 3, 30, 33, 34, 35; receipt FTR-20261027-41380592-01): in a fly model of the mitochondrial prolyl-tRNA synthetase lesion behind a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in people, pan-neuronal RNAi against GCN2 lowered the bang-sensitive fraction from about 87 to about 30 percent and RNAi against ATF4 from about 93 to about 46 percent (three vials of ten flies each; ATF4 spread about 30 to 62), and both shortened the developmental delay. Partial rescues, partial knockdowns measured in the single-RNAi lines only, seizure-like behaviour and developmental timing not separable, no compound and no ISRIB-class agent tested, no mitochondrial readout after suppression, sex not stated for the behavioural assay. It is a question-generating precedent for the ISR need, not a WWOX experiment and not a pharmacological result.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Amyloid load is the context of the fly effect; WWOX-DEE has no stated amyloid load. Adult neurodegeneration trials do not transfer to a developmental encephalopathy. The fly PARS2 precedent (the genetic precedent in the for-list) shows that an ISR can be harmful when a mitochondrial translation lesion drives it and says nothing about whether WWOX loss drives it: no link between WWOX and mitochondrial translation or OXPHOS protein abundance is established by any source read for this card.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. If the ISR were elevated and harmful, attenuation could protect function; if it is adaptive, attenuation could add harm. Neither is measured for WWOX.
p4_card.identity: ISR attenuators: eIF2B activators (ISRIB and its clinical-stage successors), PERK-arm inhibitors, and repurposed compounds that reverse eIF2 alpha-P-mediated translational repression; guanabenz as the paediatric-experience member. Full per-compound table: lucas_clarke_followup_20261026/compounds_and_sources.md section 2.1.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF a WWOX-dependent ISR elevation is shown in a human neural system. Today the transfer rests on a fly amyloid model; the one human knockout transcriptome does not show the signature. No Q230P or null-allele datum exists.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: eIF2B (five-subunit complex, EIF2B1-5, HGNC:3257-3261) or the PERK arm (EIF2AK3, HGNC:3255); direction: attenuate the ISR; context: amyloid-stressed fly neurons in the paper; UNKNOWN in WWOX-DEE.
p4_card.next_measurement: Stage 1 (decides everything after it): eIF2 alpha phosphorylation, ATF4 protein and ATF4-target transcripts in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells at matched maturity, with and without a defined proteotoxic challenge. If not elevated, park with the reopening condition below. Stage 2 (only if elevated): an eIF2B activator versus vehicle on that readout and on one functional endpoint. In the fly: an Atf4 loss-of-function arm with the Ldh and lactate readouts. Readout design (added 2026-10-27 from the fly PARS2 reading): read the eIF2 kinases separately (phospho-GCN2 and phospho-PERK, not phospho-eIF2 alpha alone), read OXPHOS subunit protein abundance as a covariate because the one precedent ISR is driven by a mitochondrial translation lesion, and keep a basal-ISR-tone control (in that precedent GCN2 RNAi alone lowered phospho-eIF2 alpha below control).
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test: no source retrieved links an ISR modulator to WWOX deficiency; coverage is DGIdb, ChEMBL, Open Targets, PubTator 3 gene censuses and eight PubMed searches on 2026-10-26, and DGIdb, ChEMBL and Open Targets are themselves empty for the eIF2B activators. A zero is a statement about those queries.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: UNKNOWN. No paediatric suitability is presumed by this card, for the candidate or for any historical authorisation of it for another use.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE (partial benefit through a downstream lever); Track A (variant-independent), Track B conditional and unmeasured.
p4_card.pharmacology: Per compound in compounds_and_sources.md: no eIF2B activity in ChEMBL for ISRIB or fosigotifator; DGIdb and Open Targets empty for the eIF2B complex; PERK inhibitors have enzyme potency in ChEMBL.

scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: Statements marked INFERENZA, including every statement about what a compound would do in WWOX-deficient tissue, are OWED a blind audit by another actor.
scope_of_checks.formal_checks: Disease-side fly rows carry verbatim locators in the manifest (104 entries; entries 31, 49, 89, 94 SUPPORTED by a blind audit, entry 95 narrowed after an OVERSHOOT finding); the compound statements are abstract-level and unaudited.
scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: No independent replication of any fly row is held; the organoid rows are one laboratory's deposit.

external_not_wwox_evidence: eIF2B-activator trial in ALS: target engaged, no clinical benefit (adults)
eIF2B activator in a mouse amyloid model: memory and tau improved, amyloid not
guanabenz in children with vanishing white matter: non-randomised benefit with frequent adverse events
PERK inhibitor in a Parkinson mouse model: neuroprotection with signs of pancreatic toxicity

p4_card.state_of_known_roads: not in the earlier hand-made series (A-D); first ISR card.
p4_card.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Compounds range from research tools to clinical-stage; availability for WWOX research is not assessed.
p4_card.value_added: Turns 'ATF4 raised' into a context-labelled need (amyloid-conditional, fly) and shows that the only signed human readout points the other way, so the first experiment is the readout, not a drug.

cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: fly neurons (Atf4 signal, whole-mount) and bulk organoid RNA; no cell-type resolution in either.
cellular_context.coverage: UNKNOWN for any WWOX system at protein level.
cellular_context.limits: The only signed human readout points the opposite way from the fly (ISR targets lower), and the fly readout needs amyloid.
cellular_context.target_expression: ISR genes are expressed in neural tissue generally; the WWOX-dependent state is UNKNOWN.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked ISR readout that a compound moves: ATF4 protein and eIF2 alpha phosphorylation (and ATF4-target transcripts) in WWOX-deficient human neural cells at matched maturity, with and without a defined proteotoxic challenge; then a functional endpoint (network, synaptic or myelin) after eIF2B activation.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX. In the fly, Atf4 signal rises only with Wwox reduction plus amyloid and Atf4 is never perturbed. In the one human knockout transcriptome the ISR target set is lower than chance (exploratory).
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly amyloid model with partial RNAi; one human knockout transcriptome without amyloid; every compound datum is from another disease, mostly adult.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF a WWOX-dependent ISR elevation is shown in a human neural system. Today the transfer rests on a fly amyloid model; the one human knockout transcriptome does not show the signature. No Q230P or null-allele datum exists.

drug_assertions.endpoint: cellular effect of stiripentol versus enzyme-level LDH inhibition
drug_assertions.measured_result_note: Cell viability and extracellular acidification fall at tens of micromolar. LDH activity in a lysate of treated cells and on recombinant enzyme falls only at hundreds of micromolar (the size of the lysate inhibition is not in the text and no LDH IC50 exists). NADH-driven oxygen consumption of isolated mouse heart and liver mitochondrial preparations, with complex I as the entry point (a flux readout of the organelle preparation, not an isolated-enzyme activity; the same paper's NADH-activity assays are dye-reduction measures), is inhibited from tens of micromolar (plot readings, auditor-confirmed, about 3 points of uncertainty: heart about 48, 5 and 1 percent remaining across the three lowest-to-highest concentrations tested; liver about 67, 36 and 23); no assay compares the two, so potencies are not comparable (INFERENZA: the effective concentrations are ordered complex I below LDH). The text figure of about 70 percent inhibition at the middle concentration is 51 to 53 percent raw in Supplementary Fig 2. The complex I paper reports no inhibition of malate dehydrogenase. Genetic LDHA/B double knockout raises respiratory capacity whereas stiripentol lowers it, so the drug does not phenocopy LDH ablation on respiration (INFERENZA). Cellular effects of stiripentol are therefore not attributable to LDH alone on the available data (the 2026 glioblastoma paper itself reports 'at least a partial role' of LDH). In a mouse glioblastoma xenograft stiripentol prolonged survival (log-rank P 0.002; median survival 80 versus 97 days, human stem-like cells in immunodeficient mice; the dose stated in the Results and legend is not stated in the Methods). None of the sources states which stereoisomer was used. Tumour models: no seizure, neurodevelopment or WWOX meaning.

evidence_against: Ldh knockdown is detrimental in other fly amyloid models (the authors' own citation).
Weak LDH inhibition by stiripentol in the retrieved measurements (a weak measure is not general inefficacy: assay, substrate level and enzyme source differ, and the 2015 report is unread).
Direct inhibition of mitochondrial complex I by stiripentol, so a metabolic effect is not an LDH effect.

An Ldh abundance rise also accompanies a complex I-reduced, ISR-activated fly model that has neither WWOX nor amyloid (DA-PARS2-LDH-001), so a raised Ldh in a Wwox-reduced fly does not by itself identify an LDH-specific lesion (INFERENZA: possible confounding by mitochondrial or ISR state).
Human lactate in WWOX deficiency reported normal or extremely low.

IT7 P3/P1 (exploratory, independently verified): in an independent WWOX-loss contrast (P47T hippocampus) the LDH isoforms split (LDHA +0.48, LDHB -0.10 against the build direction) and the six-gene module lies inside its null (p 0.060), so the LDHA elevation is not shown to be a reproducible WWOX-loss feature; the signed network and the WWOX-enriched network showed no added value for ranking compounds on this module and the signature route was not detected, not excluded, and stiripentol was outside that comparison by design. A computational result, not engagement data.

not_known: Whether lactate or LDH activity is altered in WWOX-deficient human neural cells, independent of maturity.
Whether stiripentol engages LDH in brain at tolerated exposures (the 2015 report is the claimed source and was not readable; its exposure and enzyme numbers are unknown here).
What the real potency of stiripentol on LDH is: only single-concentration measurements exist and no fitted value.
Which of stiripentol's effects on tumour-cell metabolism and respiration are LDH-mediated and which act through complex I.

Whether complex I inhibition at the exposures that matter itself recruits the integrated stress response and raises Ldh abundance in neural cells. In a fly model with reduced complex I protein, raised phospho-eIF2 alpha and an Ldh rise (DA-PARS2-LDH-001) that is the observed association and not a test; acute pharmacological inhibition is not the same perturbation, so the link is a question for the complex I arm, not a result.
Whether Ldh lowering is beneficial or harmful without the amyloid context.
Why lactate falls nominally with Wwox reduction without amyloid.

against: The Ldh rescue lacks an Ldh-alone arm, a Wwox-mRNA check and a lactate readout, and the authors cite Ldh knockdown as detrimental in other fly amyloid models.
Without amyloid lactate falls nominally and Ldh does not change.

Stiripentol inhibits LDH only weakly in the single-concentration measurements held (none gives a fitted potency, and the one at the highest concentration is the lowest), and it has other targets, including direct inhibition of mitochondrial complex I, that act at lower concentrations; any benefit would not be attributable to LDH.
LDHA in the organoid is as consistent with immaturity as with WWOX loss.
Human lactate in WWOX deficiency is reported normal or extremely low.

IT7 P3/P1 (exploratory, independently verified): in an independent WWOX-loss contrast (P47T hippocampus) the LDH isoforms split (LDHA +0.48, LDHB -0.10 against the build direction) and the six-gene module lies inside its null (p 0.060), so the LDHA elevation is not shown to be a reproducible WWOX-loss feature; the signed network and the WWOX-enriched network showed no added value for ranking compounds on this module and the signature route was not detected, not excluded, and stiripentol was outside that comparison by design. A computational result, not engagement data.

IT8 P3 (2026-10-29): the pertinence of stiripentol as a way to test the LDH node is withdrawn on primary data - two independent human-enzyme assays (7 and 9.9 percent inhibition at 2 millimolar and 500 micromolar), no LDH potency among its 28 ChEMBL rows, and a label that does not name LDH; the third report (Sada 2015) remains abstract-only and secondary.
for: Ldh RNAi improved climbing in the amyloid-plus-Wwox-reduction fly genotype (once).
Ldh transcript and lactate rise together in that genotype.

Stiripentol is an approved paediatric epilepsy drug with an LDH link published in epilepsy models (2015 report; abstract-level here) and an LDH-directed analogue series exists; nedosiran shows LDHA lowering is tolerated in humans in the liver.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: The fly effect needs amyloid; stiripentol's approved use depends on co-administration with another antiseizure drug and does not establish brain LDH engagement.

p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. A partial locomotor benefit was seen once in the fly with Ldh RNAi; no human or WWOX datum.
p4_card.identity: LDH-directed levers: stiripentol (approved for a paediatric developmental epilepsy; weak LDH inhibition in vitro), GSK2837808A and other research LDHA inhibitors, and the LDHA-directed oligonucleotide nedosiran (approved for primary hyperoxaluria, liver-directed). Per-compound table: compounds_and_sources.md section 2.2.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF lactate or LDH activity is shown to be a driver in a WWOX-deficient human neural system. The one fly precedent is amyloid-conditional; human lactate readouts in WWOX deficiency are normal or low in the cited sources (DL-BIO-008, DL-BIO-009).
p4_card.mechanism: Target: LDHA (HGNC:6535, P00338) and LDHB (HGNC:6541, P07195); direction: lower LDH activity or lactate production; context: amyloid-stressed fly head in the paper; UNKNOWN in WWOX-DEE. For stiripentol the LDH link is not the established basis of its antiseizure use.
p4_card.next_measurement: IT7 P6 2026-10-29: read LDHA and LDHB activity separately (LDHB was the discordant gene in the P47T transfer test); no computational ranking selects the compound arm. In the fly: lactate (enantiomer- or isotope-resolved) in the Ldh-RNAi double genotype, an Ldh-alone arm, and Wwox mRNA in the double line. In human neural cells: LDH activity and the lactate-to-pyruvate relationship in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic cells at matched maturity. Only then a compound arm. IT8 P3 2026-10-29: stiripentol is not carried as an LDH-engagement probe, because two independent human-enzyme assays give 7 to 9.9 percent inhibition at 0.5 to 2 millimolar (no fitted value), the US label names no LDH mechanism, and the 42 to 500 micromolar range quoted for it is a secondary figure resting on three sources; the arm is a selective LDHA tool of nanomolar potency taken from the ChEMBL human LDHA target rows (listed by ChEMBL id in pharmacological_qualification_it8_p3_20261029/measures_detail.tsv), with stiripentol kept as a complex I and GABA-A comparator so that its other pharmacology is separable from LDH. Readout design (added 2026-10-27 from the fly PARS2 reading): in every arm that perturbs complex I, read the integrated stress response (phospho-eIF2 alpha, ATF4 protein) and Ldh abundance next to Ldh ACTIVITY and lactate, because abundance, activity, metabolite level and flux are separate quantities and a complex I perturbation may raise Ldh abundance through the stress response. The designed comparison (question, model, controls, endpoint, result that would change interpretation) is in sada_ldh_precedent_p2a_20261026.md section 6; it is a proposal, nothing is authorised to run.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test: no source retrieved links an LDH inhibitor to WWOX deficiency; coverage is the six sources of compounds_and_sources.md and ten PubMed abstracts on 2026-10-26. Update 2026-10-26 (scientist-b, P2a): the 2015 report usually cited for stiripentol and LDH in epilepsy (PMID 25792327) is now identified, is paywalled with no lawful full text found, and is known here only through its abstract and three open-access secondary descriptions; it is a stiripentol-LDH precedent in epilepsy models, not a WWOX datum.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Stiripentol label: indicated for Dravet syndrome seizures in patients taking clobazam, from six months of age (openFDA label 2026-04-27); the same label means any use here would sit on top of clobazam co-therapy, an interaction this card does not assess. No paediatric suitability for WWOX-DEE is presumed.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE; Track A, Track B untested.
p4_card.pharmacology: Stiripentol: marketed formulation with a paediatric label for Dravet syndrome with clobazam; weak LDH inhibition in single-concentration enzyme measurements (no fitted potency; sizes differ between racemate, enantiomers and a database document), effective concentrations for LDH above total plasma levels and far above estimated free tissue levels in a review, other targets at lower concentrations; brain LDH engagement in vivo is asserted by secondary sources citing the 2015 report but not verified here. IT8 P3 2026-10-29 (ChEMBL molecule-first, 28 rows for the racemate, none with an LDH potency; one comparator document with LDH5 and LDH1 inhibition of 7 percent at 2 millimolar; the US label of 2026-04-27 states that the human mechanism is unknown and names GABA-A and cytochrome P450 inhibition as possible mechanisms, gives protein binding of 99 percent and no peak concentration). GSK2837808A: potent on LDHA in vitro, no in vivo or CNS datum retrieved. Nedosiran: liver-directed.
question_history: IT7 P6 (2026-10-29): the six-gene module did not transfer decisively to an independent WWOX-loss contrast and the network routes showed no added value and the signature route was not detected, not excluded (loop_demonstration_it7_p6_20261029/README.md; P3 numbers independently verified). Status, F/C/P position and the premise are unchanged.

cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: whole fly head (glia carry the highest Wwox mRNA, so neuronal origin of lactate is not established); bulk organoid RNA.
cellular_context.limits: Lactate rises only with Wwox reduction plus amyloid and falls nominally without amyloid; one human MRS datum reports lactate extremely low.
cellular_context.target_expression: LDHA and LDHB are broadly expressed; LDHC is testis-restricted by convention and absent from the organoid expression universe.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked lactate/LDH readout that a compound moves: LDH activity and the lactate-to-pyruvate relationship (enantiomer- or isotope-resolved) in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells at matched maturity; then a locomotor, network or myelin endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX in humans. Fly: a single partial locomotor rescue by Ldh RNAi in the amyloid-plus-Wwox-reduction genotype. Human knockout organoid: LDHA transcript up but confounded with maturity.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly amyloid model, whole-head metabolomics, partial RNAi; the human row is a transcript.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF lactate or LDH activity is shown to be a driver in a WWOX-deficient human neural system. The one fly precedent is amyloid-conditional; human lactate readouts in WWOX deficiency are normal or low in the cited sources (DL-BIO-008, DL-BIO-009).
